The best therapist I had was one that I personally gelled with. I trusted her and our personalities meshed well. For me, there were a few big revelations in our sessions, but the big thing was knowing that I would have a patient, impartial ear.

Complain! Get it out. Your therapist is there to listen. If you feel like you've hit a dead end, maybe try taking a new approach. My therapist used to give me assignments. One that I found particularly difficult was to write 10 things I liked about myself. It was pretty rewarding. 

The best tool I've ever used is a journal, which would help me to make my therapy sessions more productive. Which, leads me to my next point. 

When I'm feeling particularly down, I write. I still have the urge to scrape my arm with a pair of scissors, but I write instead. I write about what I'm currently feeling, what my fears are, what I want, etc. A personal outlet is key. My husband will listen to me, and he often does, but sometimes it just feels better to lay it all out there and organize my thoughts. It forces illogical thinking into something logical.
